title: Outlook mobile: duplicate a calendar event from its details on iOS and Android
summary: The briefing matches Microsoft's roadmap, rollout notice and Outlook mobile documentation. The app licensing requirements are supported, and targeted searches found no documented control for hiding Duplicate event or explanation of precisely what it copies.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Duplicate event creates a new event based on an existing event without re-entering the same details.
claims.quote: From the event details, users can select Duplicate event to quickly create a new event based on an existing event without re-entering the same details.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The user initiates duplication by selecting Duplicate event from event details.
claims.quote: We are adding the ability to duplicate an event. Simply go to the event details and select "duplicate event"

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether duplication keeps attendees, online meeting links, attachments or recurrence.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile Duplicate event copied attendees meeting link attachments recurrence invitations shared delegated calendar. Read mobile release notes and MC1492166; neither specifies copied fields. Search results gave no mobile-specific explanation.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether saving a duplicated mobile meeting invites the original attendees.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile Duplicate event copied attendees meeting link attachments recurrence invitations shared delegated calendar. Read release notes and MC1492166. Graph Create event explains invitations when attendees are included, not whether mobile duplication includes them.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented mobile duplication's shared or delegated calendar handling or destination calendar.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile Duplicate event copied attendees meeting link attachments recurrence invitations shared delegated calendar. Read release notes, MC1492166 and Graph shared/delegated calendar excerpts; none specifies the mobile duplicate option's destination or support.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft describes no new data reach for this option.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile Duplicate event copied attendees meeting link attachments recurrence invitations shared delegated calendar. Read MC1492166 and mobile release notes: they describe creating a new event from an existing one, not additional data access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft describes no new sign-in, permission or identity for Duplicate event.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile "Duplicate event" permissions sign-in identity. Read MC1492166 and mobile release notes; neither describes a new authentication or permission requirement. Search returned general authentication material, not a requirement for this option.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and api; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls; changes
claims.claim: No admin UI setting, app configuration key or automation operation specifically hides the Outlook mobile Duplicate event option in the documentation searched.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android Duplicate event disable admin Intune app configuration key Exchange PowerShell policy; Exchange Online PowerShell Outlook mobile disable "Duplicate" event OwaMailboxPolicy. Read app configuration reference; no duplicate key. OWA policy excerpts cover web/Windows.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Outlook mobile supports app settings administrators can deliver using Microsoft Intune or another UEM tool.
claims.quote: Outlook for iOS and Android supports app settings that allow unified endpoint management (UEM) administrators (using tools such as Microsoft Intune) and Microsoft 365 or Office 365 administrators to customize the behavior of the app.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: The app configuration reference includes calendar sync and calendar sharing configuration keys.
claims.quote: com.microsoft.outlook.Calendar.NativeSyncEnabled ... Setting the value to true will enable calendar sync. ... com.microsoft.outlook.Calendar.BlockSharing ... Setting the value to true will block sharing of the calendar in the app.
